findings.text: Expedited stall task reporting has a build variant that is inert: one helper reports no stalled task and another detail printer performs no action. This indicates the feature can be compiled out while keeping the call sites intact.

Expedited stall check interval derives from a tunable timeout. A zero tunable falls back to the normal stall interval converted to milliseconds. The millisecond value converted to ticks is clamped to at least two ticks and at most three hundred seconds worth of ticks, and the tunable is written back when clamping changed it. A debug build adds about twenty five percent plus one tick.

Normal stall check interval derives from a tunable expressed in seconds, clamped into the closed range three to three hundred with writeback on clamp, then scaled by the tick rate plus a fixed stall delay delta.

Stall panic path first offers the stalled mask to the scheduler layer for possible recovery and returns if handled. Otherwise it counts invocations in persistent storage and only panics after a configured count threshold when a panic-on-stall control is enabled.
A notifier helper forwards a stall event value and pointer to the CPU stall atomic notifier list and returns the chain result.

No-callback expedited cleanup wakes two grace period wait queues belonging to a node, each only if it currently has waiters. An alternate build variant provides an empty cleanup, indicating the wake step is conditional on configuration.

Sleepable RCU timing defaults are five microseconds retry check delay, one tick base delay when no expedited grace period is pending, ten ticks maximum incremental delay from slow readers, three as low mark and one thousand as high mark for default per phase no delay budget.

Unsigned clamp helpers provide low bound, high bound, and combined clamp. The adjusted per phase no delay budget corresponds to two seconds worth of ticks divided by the retry delay, clamped between the low and high marks to form the default phase budget, and the default total no delay budget is that phase budget lower bounded by one hundred. Mutable variables hold the current retry delay, phase budget, and total budget.

Reader flavor checking warns on NMI unsafe flavor use inside NMI, on multi bit flavor values, and on mismatch between requested flavor, per structure required flavor, and previously recorded per CPU flavor. The first observed per CPU flavor is installed atomically and later mismatches warn with CPU identity and old versus new values.

Sleepable RCU read lock samples the current counter set pointer, increments the calling CPU lock count for that set, orders against leaking the critical section, and returns the set index derived from the pointer. Unlock orders against leaking the critical section then increments the unlock count for the given index.

Counter set flip publishes the alternate counter set pointer with full barriers on both sides. The surrounding reasoning relies on pairing with read lock and unlock barriers and on a control dependency from the preceding equality scan to limit which readers can observe the new pointer and to aid forward progress.
A per CPU delay timer handler recovers its data record from the timer and queues that record work item on the same CPU using the grace period work queue.
Node callback scheduling walks the inclusive CPU range of the node and schedules only CPUs selected by the supplied mask bit that have been fully online, forwarding a caller supplied delay.

Sleepable RCU grace period advances under the grace period mutex through idle, first scan, and second scan states. Idle starts a new period when requested sequence exceeds current sequence. First scan requires one quiet observation before flipping counters and moving to second scan. Second scan requires two quiet observations before ending the period. A busy state causes early return for later retry.

Grace period end holds the callback mutex across sequence completion and callback scheduling to limit overlap to one extra period. It uses the usage spinlock to finish the sequence and update expedited need, then releases the grace period mutex before scheduling callbacks so one new period may start. It later reacquires the usage lock to decide on immediate restart and finally releases the callback mutex.

Grace period end uses zero callback delay for expedited periods and one tick otherwise, records end time, completes the sequence number, and raises the expedited need marker. In small configurations it schedules the boot CPU directly. In larger configurations it breadth first walks nodes under per node locks, updates have callbacks markers and expedited need, collects per CPU have callbacks masks, and schedules leaf work only when callbacks are present.

Grace period end periodically refreshes per CPU needed sequence values when they lag far behind to avoid counter wrap, starts a follow on period and reschedules without delay when work remains idle pending, and drives size growth by allocating nodes or advancing the size state release ordered unless already small or big.

Reschedule takes the usage lock, goes idle without queueing when current sequence has satisfied needed sequence, warns if a satisfied state still shows active, starts a period when a request is outstanding and state is idle, then queues delayed grace period work when not idle.

Quiet observation samples whether any delay is required under lock, then repeatedly tests the indexed reader counts. Success returns true. Failure sleeps the configured retry microseconds and retries until the supplied try count plus the no delay flag is exhausted.
Barrier callback marks itself invoked by self linking, decrements the usage barrier CPU count, and completes the barrier completion on last arrival.

Expedited current callback handling runs under the per CPU lock with idle, pending, and repost states. Idle is unexpected, pending moves to idle, repost moves back to pending and requests requeue as an expedited callback after unlock.

Callback invocation runs as work, advances the per CPU segmented callback list to the current grace period sequence under the per CPU lock, and uses an invoking flag to prevent concurrent invocation. It extracts ready callbacks, drops the lock during invocation with bottom half protection, then under lock adjusts length, clears the flag, and reschedules immediately if more ready callbacks appeared.

Grace period worker first advances state, then samples required delay under lock. Zero delay enters a same jiffy reschedule counter that forces a one tick delay after exceeding the maximum no delay budget, while nonzero delay resets the counter. It always finishes by rescheduling with the computed delay.
Interrupt work handler recovers usage and structure records, samples required delay under lock with interrupts saved, and queues grace period work with a booleanized delay.

Size state names are ordered small, alloc, wait barrier, wait call, wait callbacks one through four, big, and unknown placeholder. Boot announcement always logs the hierarchical implementation and logs configured holdoff, retry delay, and no delay values when non default plus the current maximum phase no delay value.

Observed sleepable RCU records include per structure counter pointer and per CPU data pointer, usage record with grace period sequence, needed and expedited needed sequences, callback and grace period mutexes, size state, barrier count and completion, delayed work and interrupt work, and reschedule accounting, node record with CPU range bounds and per index have callbacks state, and per CPU record with callback list, invoking flag, work, timer, CPU number, and expedited callback state.
A leak callback helper is intentionally empty and performs no reclamation, so callbacks routed to it are silently dropped.
